key_findings: One index patient: a 48-year-old medically free man with a thyroglossal duct cyst, managed conservatively. After 1.6 years, follow-up ultrasound found a left thyroid nodule; FNA showed Bethesda VI papillary carcinoma. He had total thyroidectomy, the Sistrunk procedure and central neck dissection. Histology showed classical papillary carcinoma (T1bN0aM0, 1.2 cm), and the TGDC was free of carcinoma. He was discharged on day three on levothyroxine 150 mg (printed unit kept, ambiguity), with an unremarkable follow-up.

Figures 1 and 2 print "RT CERV LN"/"Dist 0.445 cm" and "Rt Lobe", which match neither the captions nor the text (5 x 8 mm midline lesion; left lobe nodule). Each asset sits in its own figure slot, so this is a caption-to-image mismatch, recorded as a limitation; patient attribution stays with the captions.

T1bN0aM0 is kept literal (N0a as printed) with no staging system. "No cervical lymphadenopathy" is a negative imaging observation. The follow-up 5 x 8 mm midline lesion is kept separate from the initial cyst and the CT lesion (ambiguity).
Levothyroxine "discharged on" has action unknown (ruling). The "Follow-up" time with a null anchor applies to the follow-up examination, US, CT and TFT facts.
